_comment: Kruti Dev 010 <-> Unicode ground truth. `rt: false` marks pairs whose legacy spelling is non-canonical, so unicode->kruti will produce a different (equally valid) spelling and round-trip equality is not expected.

split_matra.why: o-matra is typed as aa + e
au-matra is typed as aa + ai

i_matra.why: THE headline case: i-matra is typed first
i-matra hops over ha, then half-na

reph.why: reph is typed AFTER the cluster it crowns
reph after a two-char full consonant
reph AND i-matra interacting - the hard one

rakar_and_conjuncts.why: half-ba + rakar collapses the double halant
ksha is half `{` + vertical bar `k`, like bha/sha
i-matra + ksha + aa, all three at once
bare `{` is the HALF form क्ष्, no bar
reported broken: ष्ट्र + भाषा in one word
reported broken: i-matra then the doubled न्न
reported broken: anusvara, half-sa, kri ligature, i-matra, split o-matra
doubled त्त is half-ta + ta + bar, no dedicated glyph
doubled द्ध, which DOES have a dedicated glyph - on `)`, not `}` (that one is द्व)
द्ध glyph then an i-matra that has to hop it
doubled न्न after an independent vowel

rakar_variants.why: `ª` is the rakar used under stemless ta/tha/da/dha - was leaking a raw Latin-1 byte
alternate pra glyph; reverse still prefers the `iz` spelling
kri ligature after a half consonant

anusvara_order.why: nasal is typed AFTER the matra
THE regression: i-matra AND nasal in one word. Used to reverse to `gafnh` -> हंदिी
i-matra hops over sa while the nasal stays put

punctuation.why: double danda beats single (longest match). Written attached to the word, as it always is in practice - a bare 'AA' token is indistinguishable from an acronym
THE comma regression. The comma is the `]` key; `,` is ए, so a literal comma used to come back as हैए
ए and a real comma in the same line, which is the whole ambiguity
the full stop is the `-` key, not `.` (which is ण्)
semicolon is the `(` key; the ASCII `(` still reverses to `¼`
slash is the `@` key, not `/` (which is ध्)
both double-quote slots fold onto the one ASCII quote

english_safe.why: word-list English and a bare number survive
decimals survive; the dot would otherwise become half-na
